2. The facts of the case are that the petitioner Mohammad Abul Kalam, filed a complaint on 21-9-2002 before the learned Magistrate, First class, Chittagong under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure stating, inter alia, that the petitioner is the owner of the schedule land and his father purchased the scheduled land vide registered sake deed dated 23-6-1965; that in the name of the petitioner's father BS Khatian has been rightly recorded and that the opposite parties are trying to bring earth filing the land to construct shop upon the schedule land. It is further stated that there is apprehension of breach of peace which may cause bloodshed and murder and that the petitioner stating apprehension of breach of peace also made a GD entry with Lohagara police station being GD No. 670 dated 17-9-2002 and prayed to draw proceeding under section 145 of Criminal Procedure Code against the opposite parties. 

 11. It is further submitted that the learned Revisional Court mostly relied on the deeds of the opposite parties dated 17-4-1957 and 14-11-1961 on the plea that these deeds are earlier than that of the petitioner's father's deed which is not true because by virtue of those deeds the opposite parties never came into possession and their names have not been recorded in BS khatian and as the petitioner was in possession his father name rightly recorded in BS khatian and that the appointment of Receiver is an equitable order by which there is no scope to be prejudiced and to maintain law and order in the locality and also to protect the property of rightful owner, appointment or receiver is very much essential and as such the learned Revisional Court committed serious error of law in holding that the opposite parties are in possession and therefore the revisional order is an abuse of process and is liable to be set aside. 

 15. On perusal of the record, it appears that the opposite parties claim 20 decimals of land from disputed plot, which they acquired by way of 2 registered kabalas, dated 17-4-1957 and 14-11-1961. Father of the petitioner, Md Abdul Kalam, the long after the purchase of opposite parties, purchased 7 decimals of land by a kabala dated 23-6-1965 and thereafter gifted the same to his son on 25-3-1990 who is petitioner in the instant case. It is alleged that the father of the petitioner has not gifted the land of plot No. 14083 to his son and the name of the petitioner's father has been wrongly inserted in BS Khatian.
